classification.difficultyReason: Construct three different tight-wrap cross-sectional decompositions from tangent-circle arrangements, combine triangle/rectangle and sector areas with Pythagoras, extrude by the fixed height and compare. The prompts name only arrangements and desired volumes, so the multi-step geometric models must be selected independently; no general proof or novel theorem is required.

content.prompt: The cylindrical canisters have radius $2.5\text{ cm}$ and height $20\text{ cm}$. They must be packaged in one layer with tight shrink-wrap.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Suppose that the six canisters are packed in a row. What is the total volume of the package? Calculate your answer to 3 decimal places.

spec.description: Six touching circles in one row and their tight enclosing boundary.
spec.mathematics: Two straight tangents and two semicircular ends.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated package dimensions or areas supplied.

answer.worked:
The cross-section is a $25\text{ cm}\times5\text{ cm}$ rectangle with two semicircular ends of radius $2.5$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}A&=25\times5+\pi\left(\frac52\right)^2\\A&=125+\frac{25\pi}{4}\text{ cm}^2\\V&=20\left(125+\frac{25\pi}{4}\right)\\V&=2500+125\pi\text{ cm}^3\\V&\approx2892.699\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Suppose that the six canisters are packed in two rows of three. What is the total volume of the package? Calculate your answer to 3 decimal places.

spec.description: Six tangent circles in two aligned rows of three, enclosed by straight tangents and rounded corners.

answer.worked:
Start with the outer $15\text{ cm}\times10\text{ cm}$ rectangle. Replace its four $2.5$ cm corner squares with four quarter-circles.
$$\begin{align*}A&=15\times10-4\left(\frac52\right)^2+\pi\left(\frac52\right)^2\\A&=125+\frac{25\pi}{4}\text{ cm}^2\\V&=20\left(125+\frac{25\pi}{4}\right)\\V&=2500+125\pi\text{ cm}^3\\V&\approx2892.699\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Suppose that the six canisters are packed as shown in the diagram opposite. What is the total volume of the package? Calculate your answer to 3 decimal places.

spec.description: Six tangent circles arranged in rows of three, two and one; three straight tangent segments join arcs around the corner circles.
spec.mathematics: Equilateral triangle of corner centres with side four radii, three strips and corner sectors totalling a circle.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated lengths or areas supplied.

answer.worked:
The three corner centres form an equilateral triangle of side $10$ cm. Its height follows from Pythagoras' theorem. Around it are three $10\text{ cm}\times2.5\text{ cm}$ strips and three $120^\circ$ sectors, together one circle.
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=10^2-5^2\\h&=5\sqrt3\text{ cm}\\A&=\frac12\times10\times5\sqrt3+3\times10\times\frac52+\pi\left(\frac52\right)^2\\A&=25\sqrt3+75+\frac{25\pi}{4}\text{ cm}^2\\V&=20\left(25\sqrt3+75+\frac{25\pi}{4}\right)\\V&=500\sqrt3+1500+125\pi\text{ cm}^3\\V&\approx2758.724\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Which is the best packaging: a, b or c?

answer.worked: The triangular arrangement has the smallest total package volume: $2758.724\text{ cm}^3$, compared with $2892.699\text{ cm}^3$ for each of the other two arrangements.
